claimed_purpose.text: SimpleMem compresses dialogues into atomic, timestamped memory units using an LLM-driven approach
SQLiteStorage manages a SQLite database specifically for cross-session memory persistence.
Stores conversations as atomic, self-contained facts rather than raw transcripts
Described as a lifelong memory system for LLM agents

mechanisms.text: Retrieve policy: intent-aware, adaptive-depth retrieval planning — the LLM generates a retrieval plan inferring latent search intent to dynamically determine retrieval scope and depth, rather than fixed-depth retrieval

Session finalization (write path): extracts observations from recorded events, optionally runs SimpleMem 3-stage pipeline to produce rich memory entries, generates a session summary, and persists everything to storage

The HTTP server is implemented in MCP/server/http_server.py and uses FastAPI/Starlette with CORS middleware; allowed methods include GET, POST, DELETE — suggesting memories can be created, read, and deleted via HTTP
Curated memory write via structured compression, not raw log accumulation: interactions are distilled into compact, self-contained facts with resolved coreferences and absolute timestamps
Online deduplication during write path: related context within a session is merged into unified abstract representations, removing redundancy as memory is built rather than at query time
ON DELETE CASCADE on all child tables (session_events, observations, session_summaries) means deleting a session record removes all its associated events, observations, and summaries.
The store records are scoped with a persons field (array) and an entities field (array), implying per-entity or per-person isolation within the store.
Storage layer combines dense vector search, full-text search, and structured metadata handling built around LanceDB, Tantivy, and SQL metadata
Reflection can be disabled per-query via an override parameter, documented as useful for adversarial questions that should not use reflection
Memory entries are written to a vector store via add_entries; the write path goes dialogue buffer → LLM extraction → VectorStore.add_entries.
Each distinct memory is isolated by a separate table_name, allowing multiple independent memory stores within one LanceDB database.
SimpleMem involves a memory generation phase and a memory search/retrieval phase, both of which contribute to token consumption.
MemoryBuilder uses a sliding-window approach over input dialogues (window_size, overlap_size settings) before storing
The MCP server stores API keys in encrypted form, with an encryption key configurable via environment variable.
Omni-SimpleMem uses selective ingestion (entropy-driven filtering per modality) to control what is persisted
Entries carry a valid_from timestamp and an importance score used to drive decay and prune decisions.
Multi-tenant isolation: each tenant's memories are stored and retrieved independently via tenant_id.
MCP server enforces per-user data isolation via per-user data tables and token authentication
All deletions are soft: entries are marked as superseded rather than physically removed.
Two persistent stores: SQLite for structured records and LanceDB for vector embeddings
v3 introduces Online Semantic Synthesis as an architectural change
Retrieval is described as an intent-aware 3-stage pipeline
